messages.text:
Marvelous, go ahead with the long strips, again split in barrel and end cap PRs.

The material between the sandwich sensors should not only act as the cooling and local mount, it is of course also the stave itself (design a structure how they are fixed and determine for the barrel how many anchor points are needed to prevent sagging). 

Cable and cooling routing should also be defined.

I’ll develop the long-strip barrel and endcap in separate PRs. I’ll treat the sandwich core as the load-bearing stave, size the barrel’s support spacing against sag, and define the mounting, cooling and cable routes before building the prototypes.

I’m using the acts-spack skill to verify the local DD4hep and Geant4 environment. The long-strip study uses two separately read out stereo sensors; I’ll retain that measurement model and replace the provisional support space with an explicit structural sandwich, mounting seats and routed services.

The Spack preflight reports changed setup and lockfile fingerprints, so I’ll verify the installed runtime directly before using it. There’s also a mechanical conflict to resolve: the old 5 mm sensor separation cannot hold the full cooled CFRP sandwich. I’ll document the required separation and calculate support spacing from bending, core shear and the complete stave load.

The selected long-strip baseline has two barrel layers at 840 and 1060 mm, and six discs per end at radii 786–1108 mm. I’m preserving those as the comparison envelope. The new model will use a continuous cooled sandwich between the sensors, with outward lifts where modules overlap, and paired mounting contacts to resist stave twist.

The first structural calculation is dominated by core shear, so a bending-only estimate would understate sag. With the full stave load, a 5 MPa core shear modulus and twice nominal gravity, the current proposal recommends 17 support stations at 163.75 mm spacing. I’ll now check the mounting webs, paired sensors and services in the native geometry.

The paired-plane coverage check found why the inherited row spacing is insufficient: oblique 1 GeV tracks can cross one sensor but miss its partner. I’m increasing the overlap using the stereo separation and worst incidence angle as the design basis, while retaining the failed layout as a control. The routing ledger also shows that the fixed 25 mm trunk fails the adverse packing scenario.

The revised layout greatly reduces the sampled pair misses, though some remain and will stay visible in the report. The native overlap check is taking too long with every component in one flat assembly. I’m grouping components by stave so the same geometry and overlap tolerance can be checked efficiently.

The grouped native check now runs successfully. It found a real clearance problem: the mounting webs cross neighbouring cores. I’m moving them to the free shingle edge and moving the buses and hybrids to the opposite edge. I’ll also distinguish the oversized cable benchmark from a conductor-sized routing proposal, with voltage-drop and warm-resistivity checks.

The corrected barrel geometry has passed the native check with zero overlaps, and Geant4 saved complete stereo-pair hits in both layers. The conservative support screen calls for at least 15 stations; I recommend 17 to leave margin for the declared modulus and load assumptions. I’m completing an independent multispan beam calculation, then proceeding to the separate endcap design.

[Barrel PR #52](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/52) is open. For the endcap, I’m developing four rings of stereo pairs on continuous cooled petal carriers. The inner mounting region is tight against the short-strip service trunk, so I’ll keep the full model outside that corridor. I’ll also compare the shifted first disc against the original datum to show any coverage loss.

The barrel PR is open with 17 support stations per stave. The first endcap check found collisions between neighbouring electronics and between the internal webs and cable collectors. I’m correcting those passive components before repeating the geometry checks; the sensor layout stays fixed.

The proposed endcap has four rings on 12 cooled structural petals per disc, with one inner and two outer mounting contacts per petal. The gravity screen supports the installed orientation, but horizontal handling needs a temporary frame. The combined barrel/endcap services fit the reference packing case; the case with reduced space and added spare capacity still fails within the fixed corridor.

The endcap now passes the overlap and ROOT persistence checks. A routing review also showed that three cooling loops leave long heat paths near the petal edges. I’m increasing this to six distributed U-loops per petal and assigning each complete sensor pair to its nearest loop, then checking the additional service load.

The revised sensors and services clear the geometry check at 10⁻⁵ mm. The coverage study also finds tracks lost by moving the first disc to clear the barrel collector; those losses will be shown in the PR. The thermal screens remain inconclusive: they span from a small through-thickness temperature rise to a failing lateral heat-path estimate, so cooling still needs simulation and qualification.

Both endcap Geant4 runs passed: each signed end saved both sensor faces of the same module in all six discs. I’m preparing the separate endcap PR with the drawings, routes and validation receipts. It will retain the first-disc coverage losses, handling and thermal failures, and service-packing limits for review.

The designs and local checks are complete, and I’m publishing the endcap PR stacked on the barrel PR. The barrel recommendation is 17 stations per stave with two fasteners at each station. The endcap will include the three-contact mounting concept and six-loop routing, with coverage, thermal and handling limitations called out.

[Endcap PR #53](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/53) is now open, stacked on [barrel PR #52](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/52). Both include TDR-style drawings and retained validation evidence. I’m checking hosted CI and synchronizing the shared journal; this active turn’s final token counters are still unavailable.

Final review caught a problem in the bus model: the copper foil had insulation on only one face. I’m adding a full dielectric wrap, keeping the connection between the spine and collector, and rerunning the passive-material and transport checks before closing out.

The fully wrapped bus model passes the fresh geometry, persistence and Geant4 checks. Its added material is included in the revised 1.497 kg petal load. The barrel’s hosted build has passed; I’m finishing the endcap closeout and hosted validation.

The final updates are pushed and their hosted checks are running. Both PRs and your primary checkout have the same shared journal; validation passed for 119 task records and 124 primary records. The primary branch and scientific files are unchanged.

The endcap now has ten passing local controls, including a check of the dielectric wrap and bus junction. The sensor positions and IDs are unchanged by that correction. The remaining step is the final hosted validation.
Hosted CI has passed the detector controls, including the new long-strip tests. It is now finishing the documentation checks and dashboard build. The local native checks remain successful.

Opened two draft PRs:

- [#52 — Barrel](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/52): continuous structural staves, defined cooling/cable routes, and **17 support stations per stave**, with two fasteners each. The declared sag model requires at least 15; 17 predicts approximately **36 µm including the joint allowance**.
- [#53 — Endcap](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/53): structural petals, three-contact mounting, six cooling loops per petal, fully insulated buses and cumulative service routing.

Both include drawings and passed native DD4hep, ROOT, Geant4 and final hosted CI checks. Endcap coverage losses, thermal qualification, handling and adverse service packing remain documented review items.

The shared journal is synchronized. This active turn’s final token counters remain pending.
